attributes.axis_log: BASELINE re-derived live: real 26, insns 747/747, multiset IDENTICAL. AXIS 1 all three NULL arms spelled ei-relative: real 26 -> 54, reproducing the prior record's number EXACTLY; crucially the three immediate differences DISAPPEAR and the whole remaining diff is register fields. AXIS 2 two-site subset (p1140+p1152 only, p1068 left as a pointer store): real 42; p1068 keeps its correct r23 but p960 falls to r19. AXIS 3 axis-1 plus declaration-order permutation of the twelve pointer locals to [.. 1152, 1140, 960, 972, 1068 ..]: real 54 -> 48, the smallest register-only residual found, and the variant retained as the rule base. AXIS 4 axis-2 plus demoting p960 in declaration order: real 42, IDENTICAL to axis 2, so the decl-order axis is inert in that cell. FALSIFICATION OF THE PRIOR FRAMING: attempt.initeffects-value-identity-recolor-l3 explained the cascade as 'converting drops p1068 from 3 references to 2, re-ranking it against its 11 siblings'. That is WRONG. Reading every register reference in the TARGET stream (fnasm, whole function) shows retail's r23/r20/r19 each have exactly TWO uses (0x5e8+0x5ec, 0x650+0x654, 0x6b0+0x6b4) - the same counts our converted source emits. Retail reaches r19=1152/r20=1140/r21=960/r22=972/r23=1068 with our use counts, so the ranking is NOT a function of use count or declaration order and is not source-reachable; five distinct cells confirm it.
